Entries.Text: Find dummies, materials, bones, meshes and model headers with a filter, then edit or delete every match at once. Find on the first tab, then preview and apply on the second.
Edit or delete the objects found, with a preview of every change.
Where to look for the objects.
The objects selected in the loaded model. Selecting the model root picks its header.
Every object of the loaded model.
Every model in the loaded model's file, such as a part or DS2 map binder that holds several.
Every model in the project, or in one Source List list. Each file is read, so this can take a while.
Load a model to use this scope.
Select a dummy, material, bone, mesh or the model root first.
Match the model name, its file name or its alias. Leave empty for every model in the scope.
The kind of object and its name: a bone or material by name, a dummy by reference ID, or a mesh by position. With Any, the text also matches the kind.
Each condition must be met by one of the object's fields. Empty conditions are ignored.
The field that must contain the value, by its path (Textures[0].Path, BoundingBox.Min) or part of it. Leave empty for any field.
Add a condition. Every condition must be met.
How the text inputs are matched.
Find the objects, or start over.
Find every object that matches the filter. Nothing changes until you click Apply on the Edit tab.
The objects the edit applies to. Click one to jump to it.
The filter or the scope's selection changed since Find. Find again to edit the current matches.
Find the objects to edit on the Find tab first.
Models that aren't loaded are edited directly. These edits can't be undone and are written with Save All.
What to do to the matches.
Each step sets a field. Steps run in order, each on the result of the step before. An object that a step can't apply to is left completely unchanged.
The field to set. Only settable fields of the objects found are listed.
Add a step, run after the others.
The value the operator uses. Use a dot for decimals.
Set the value. A vector takes one number per component.
Add to the value. A vector takes one number for every component, or one per component.
Subtract from the value. A vector takes one number for every component, or one per component.
Multiply the value. A vector takes one number for every component, or one per component.
Divide the value. Dividing by zero skips the object.
Raise the value to the given number if it is lower.
Lower the value to the given number if it is higher.
Flip the value: true becomes false, and false becomes true.
Replace every occurrence of the text (not case-sensitive), such as part of a texture path.
Every change Apply will make, calculated from the steps. Click one to jump to its object.
Pick a field in a step to see the changes.
The matches are out of date. Find again before applying.
Make every listed change. A loaded model's changes are one undo step; models that aren't loaded are left unsaved.
Replace needs the text to find
The operator doesn't apply to this field
{0} is kept with its history in a view. Load it to edit it.
Bone links can only be changed in a loaded model, which keeps the hierarchy in sync.
A model header can't be deleted.
Objects can only be deleted from loaded models.
{0} objects changed or were removed since Find, and were skipped.
{0} models that aren't loaded were changed and are unsaved. Use {1} to write them.
Find again to make another edit.
Mass edit: applied to {0} objects, {1} stale, {2} skipped.
The objects Delete removes. Click one to jump to it.
Only objects in loaded models are deleted, as one undo step in each view. Indices that point at deleted bones and materials are updated, like deleting in Contents.
Delete every match in a loaded model.
Delete {0} objects? Bones are deleted with their child bones. Undo restores them.
Mass edit: deleted {0} objects, {1} stale, {2} skipped.
Fill in the Mass Edit filter from this search and find the objects there, so you can edit or delete them all at once.
